verdict.rationale: Yapily's API clearly supports creating consent/link sessions, retrieving balances/transactions, and managing connections (yapily-docs-2, -7, -9, -15), and there is an MCP surface (yapily-docs-6, yapily-probe-3) — but that MCP is documented as connecting coding agents (Claude/Cursor) to the documentation, not as an operational interface for agents to actually invoke banking actions with scoped credentials. Missing for 10: evidence of an MCP tool surface that performs live API calls (link sessions, balance/transaction retrieval) rather than just docs access, and explicit scoped-credential/agent-auth model for such calls.
